title: Homogeneous determinant locus and its normalized affine chart rings
statement:
Let $N,r$ be integers with $0<r<N$, and let $\mathcal I$ be the increasing $r$-subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. Put $B=\mathbf Z[p_J:J\in\mathcal I]$, with every $p_J$ of degree one [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For an arbitrary ordered $r$-tuple, let $p_{j_1\ldots j_r}$ be the sorting sign times the corresponding increasing coordinate, or zero if indices repeat. For $I,K\in\mathcal I$ define
$$C_{I,K}(a,b)=p_{i_1\ldots i_{a-1}k_bi_{a+1}\ldots i_r},\qquad F_{I,K}=p_I^{r-1}p_K-\det C_{I,K}.$$
Here determinants use [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. Put $H=(F_{I,K}:I,K\in\mathcal I)$, $A=B/H$ with its induced grading [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and $X=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ [def-pc-proj], with $U_I=D_+(p_I)$. On $U_I$ let $M^{(I)}$ be the $r\times N$ matrix with identity columns indexed by $I$ and off-pivot entries
$$x^{(I)}_{aj}=p_{i_1\ldots i_{a-1}ji_{a+1}\ldots i_r}/p_I\quad(j\notin I).$$
Every $F_{I,K}$ is homogeneous of degree $r$, and for every commutative ring $R$ and $r\times N$ matrix $M$ over $R$, evaluation $p_J\mapsto\det M_J$ annihilates all $F_{I,K}$, including when the pivot minors are zero divisors. The graded quotient induces a closed immersion
$$j:X\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Proj}(B)=\mathbf P^{\binom Nr-1}_{\mathbf Z}$$
[def-weil-closed-immersion, def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. The $U_I$ cover $X$, and the homomorphism
$$\mathbf Z[X_{aj}:1\leq a\leq r,\ j\notin I]\longrightarrow A_{(p_I),0},\qquad X_{aj}\longmapsto x^{(I)}_{aj}$$
is an isomorphism. Its inverse sends each $p_J/p_I$ to the $J$-minor of the matrix with identity columns at $I$ and entries $X_{aj}$ elsewhere. In particular $\det M^{(I)}_J=p_J/p_I$ for every $J$, and $U_I$ is affine space of dimension $r(N-r)$ with these exact coordinate functions.

proof.text: Each ordered coordinate is zero or a signed degree-one variable. Thus each product in the Leibniz expansion of $\det C_{I,K}$ has degree $r$, as does $p_I^{r-1}p_K$, and $F_{I,K}$ is homogeneous (zero is allowed). The ideal $H$ is homogeneous: if $h=\sum_{I,K}b_{I,K}F_{I,K}$, its degree-$d$ component is $\sum_{I,K}(b_{I,K})_{d-r}F_{I,K}$, taking negative components to be zero. Consequently $A_d$ is the image of $B_d$ in $B/H$; these images form a direct sum since every homogeneous component of an element of $H$ is in $H$. Products respect degrees. This constructs the asserted quotient grading and makes $B\twoheadrightarrow A$ degree preserving.

source.place: Agent completion of the homogeneous determinant presentation underlying the normalized charts of Tag 089T (lemma-gkn-representable).

proof.text:
Let $M$ be an $r\times N$ matrix over an arbitrary commutative ring $R$, and fix increasing $I,K$. Set $P=M_I$ and $Q=M_K$. Under evaluation by maximal minors, the $(a,b)$ entry of $C_{I,K}$ is $\det(P[a\leftarrow M_{k_b}])$. Indeed sorting columns multiplies the determinant by the sorting sign; repeated columns give zero by pairing the Leibniz summands with the transposition of those columns. By the column-replacement formula of [lem-sfb-matrix-cramer-determinant-identities], the evaluated matrix is $\operatorname{adj}(P)Q$. The two determinant formulas of that node give
$$\det(\operatorname{adj}(P)Q)=\det(\operatorname{adj}(P))\det Q=(\det P)^{r-1}\det Q.$$
This is exactly evaluation of $F_{I,K}=0$. It holds without division or cancellation, for every $I,K$, so polynomial evaluation annihilates $H$ even when a pivot minor is a zero divisor.

source.place: Agent determinant-coordinate completion of Tag 089T, using the cited Cramer identities (Mathlib Matrix.cramer_eq_adjugate_mulVec, Matrix.det_adjugate and Matrix.det_mul).

proof.text: Apply the surjective graded-map clause (3) of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] in its affine-base case to $B\twoheadrightarrow A$. Its affine restriction clause (1) identifies these Proj schemes with the absolute Proj schemes in the item. This gives the canonical closed immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Proj}(B)$. The target is the specified projective space by [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], with its homogeneous coordinates indexed by $\mathcal I$. The images of the variables generate the irrelevant ideal of $A$: every positive-degree monomial has a variable factor. Therefore [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open] gives the covering $X=\bigcup_I U_I$ and the canonical identifications $U_I=\operatorname{Spec}(A_{(p_I),0})$.

source.place: Tag 01N0 (lemma-surjective-graded-rings-map-proj), affine-base case; Tag 01M4 (lemma-standard-open), standard chart identifications and covering.

proof.text: Fix $I$, and put $E=A_{(p_I),0}$ and $z_J=p_J/p_I\in E$, so $z_I=1$. By [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], every element of $E$ is $a/p_I^n$ for a homogeneous $a\in A_n$. Lift $a$ to $b\in B_n$ using the quotient grading from Step 1. Expanding $b$ as a sum of degree-$n$ monomials shows that $a/p_I^n$ is the corresponding integer polynomial in the $z_J$: a monomial $p_{J_1}\cdots p_{J_n}/p_I^n$ is $z_{J_1}\cdots z_{J_n}$. Thus the $z_J$ generate $E$ over $\mathbf Z$, including its degree-zero constants. This uses only the fraction relation and the polynomial expansion, and requires no regularity of $p_I$.

source.place: Agent explicit homogeneous-fraction calculation on the standard chart of Tag 01M4.

proof.text:
For the matrix $M^{(I)}$ of the item, its entry at $(a,j)$, including $j\in I$, equals $p_{i_1\ldots i_{a-1}ji_{a+1}\ldots i_r}/p_I$: this is $1$ if $j=i_a$, and zero for the other pivot columns because an index repeats. Hence the entries of its $J$-submatrix are precisely $C_{I,J}(a,b)/p_I$. Expanding the determinant and combining the $r$ denominators gives
$$\det M^{(I)}_J=\frac{\det C_{I,J}}{p_I^r}=\frac{p_I^{r-1}p_J}{p_I^r}=z_J.$$
The middle equality is $F_{I,J}=0$ in $A$; the last is equality of localization fractions. In particular every $z_J$ is an integer polynomial in the off-pivot entries of $M^{(I)}$.

source.place: Agent normalized-minor calculation completing the normalized affine charts in Tag 089T; fraction convention of Tag 01M4.

proof.text: Put $D=\mathbf Z[X_{aj}:1\leq a\leq r,\ j\notin I]$ and let $T$ be the $r\times N$ matrix over $D$ with identity columns at $I$ and off-pivot entries $X_{aj}$. Evaluation $p_J\mapsto d_J=\det T_J$ is a ring map $B\to D$. Step 2, with $R=D$ and $M=T$, says that it kills every $F_{L,K}$ and hence $H$. It therefore descends to $e:A\to D$, by $e([b])=b(d_J)$; changing $b$ by an element of $H$ changes this value by zero. Since $e(p_I)=\det(1_r)=1$, define $A[1/p_I]\to D$ by $a/p_I^n\mapsto e(a)$. This is well defined: a relation $p_I^k(ap_I^m-bp_I^n)=0$ evaluates to $e(a)-e(b)=0$; addition and multiplication follow from the fraction formulas. Restricting gives $\psi:E\to D$, with $\psi(z_J)=d_J$.

source.place: Agent construction of the inverse chart homomorphism by the polynomial, quotient and localization definitions; the determinant identity used here was proved in Step 2.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], evaluation $X_{aj}\mapsto x^{(I)}_{aj}$ defines $\phi:D\to E$. The determinant of the identity matrix with its $a$-th column replaced by the $j$-th column of $T$ is $X_{aj}$: every other identity column forces its corresponding row in the Leibniz product. Sorting this ordered minor supplies exactly the sign in the ordered-coordinate convention. Thus $\psi\phi(X_{aj})=X_{aj}$, and polynomial homomorphism uniqueness gives $\psi\phi=1_D$. Conversely $\phi\psi(z_J)=\det M^{(I)}_J=z_J$ by Step 5, since evaluating the Leibniz polynomial commutes with its finite sums and products. The generation proved in Step 4 gives $\phi\psi=1_E$. These are the required inverse homomorphisms, with the claimed formula on every $p_J/p_I$. Together with Step 3 this identifies $U_I$ with $\operatorname{Spec}D$, affine $r(N-r)$-space over $\mathbf Z$, and identifies its exact coordinate functions with the displayed $x^{(I)}_{aj}$.
